The cashier has become an important part of daily life. The experience taught Jack more than any book could. Sometimes a short talk can solve a big problem. What's more, at times the queue moved very slowly.
What matters most is not speed, but keeping on. Jack thanked Tom for the honest advice. Tom advised Jack to try singing as a new hobby. For example, the bouquet hints at pear and honey.

There are always more possibilities than we expect. They talked about everything from schoolwork to future dreams. Tom and Jack are preparing a report about the fruit shop. In fact, an extended warranty adds three years.

Jack is saving money to buy a ticket to Chengdu. There is still a long way to go, but the direction is right. People around Jack often share different ideas about the fruit shop. For example, heavy rain forced the postponement of the outdoor concert.
On Friday evenings, Jack reviews the notes from class. Little by little, things began to change. Jack believes that trying new things keeps life fresh.
